exercises.name: Bird Dog

setup.text: Start on your hands and knees with your spine in a neutral position.

instructions.text: Slowly reach one arm forward while extending the opposite leg behind you. Pause briefly, focusing on keeping your hips level and your torso still. Return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.cues: Move slowly and focus on control rather than speed.
exercises.notes: This exercise challenges your balance and coordination by teaching you to stabilize your core while your limbs work independently.

exercises.name: Half-Moon Hinge
exercises.description: Hip hinge pattern with lateral reach

setup.text: Begin in a tall kneeling position with your hips stacked over your knees and your arms relaxed at your sides.

instructions.text: Hinge at the hips and sweep one arm overhead in a wide arc, tracing a half moon. Keep your ribs down and your hips square as you reach. Return to tall kneeling and repeat on the other side.

exercises.cues: Reach long through the fingertips; avoid collapsing at the waist.
exercises.notes: Pairs well with other floor work since it needs no equipment change.

exercises.name: Dead Bug

setup.text: Lie on your back with your arms reaching toward the ceiling and your knees bent above your hips.

instructions.text: Press your lower back gently into the floor. Slowly lower one arm overhead while extending the opposite leg toward the floor. Stop before your back arches, then return to the start and switch sides.

exercises.cues: Keep your lower back flat throughout; move only as far as you can control.
exercises.notes: A foundational core exercise that teaches bracing under limb movement.

exercises.name: Forearm Plank

setup.text: Set your forearms on the floor beneath your shoulders and extend your legs behind you into a straight line.

instructions.text: Hold the position with your hips level, squeezing your glutes and bracing your abdominals. Breathe steadily for the duration of the hold.

exercises.cues: Don't let your hips sag or pike; keep a straight line from head to heel.
exercises.notes: A timed hold, so the app will count down aloud.

exercises.name: Kneel to Stand With Medicine Ball

setup.text: Start in a tall kneeling position with a weight held overhead. Keep your arms in line with your ears and your torso straight.

instructions.text: Step one foot forward into a lunge position, then drive through your front leg to stand. Keep the weight overhead and your upper body steady throughout the movement. Reverse the motion to return to the starting position.

exercises.cues: Maintain steady core; don't lean forward.
exercises.notes: This challenges balance and stability while reinforcing the strength needed to hold a tight streamline.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat

setup.text: Stand with your feet slightly wider than your hips, holding a weight close to your chest with both hands.

instructions.text: Sit your hips back and down, keeping your chest tall and your elbows inside your knees at the bottom. Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.

exercises.cues: Keep your heels down and your knees tracking over your toes.
exercises.notes: The weight at your chest acts as a counterbalance and helps you sit deeper.

exercises.name: Suspension Row
exercises.description: Horizontal pull for the upper back

setup.text: Hold the suspension handles and walk your feet forward so your body leans back at an angle with your arms extended.

instructions.text: Pull your chest toward the handles by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together. Lower yourself under control until your arms are straight again.

exercises.cues: Keep your body in one straight line; don't let your hips drop.
exercises.notes: Walk your feet farther forward to make it harder.

exercises.name: Suspension Chest Fly
exercises.description: Chest and shoulder stability under load

setup.text: Face away from the anchor point holding the handles, arms extended in front of your chest, body leaning forward on your toes.

instructions.text: Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, lowering your chest between the handles. Keep a soft bend in your elbows, then press back to the starting position.

exercises.cues: Brace your core so your hips don't sag as you open your arms.
exercises.notes: Shares a configuration with the suspension row, so run them back to back.

exercises.name: Suspension Hamstring Curl

setup.text: Lie on your back with your heels resting in the suspension straps and your arms flat at your sides.

instructions.text: Lift your hips into a bridge, then pull your heels toward your glutes by bending your knees. Keep your hips high the entire time, then extend your legs back out slowly.

exercises.cues: Don't let your hips drop when your legs extend.
exercises.notes: Requires lowering the straps, so the app will announce the transition.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Plank Rollout

setup.text: Begin in a plank position with your forearms on a stability ball and your body forming a straight line from head to heel.

instructions.text: Slowly roll the ball forward by extending your arms, maintaining a rigid torso throughout the movement. Roll out as far as you can while keeping good alignment, then pull the ball back to the starting position.

exercises.cues: Keep your core tight; don't let your hips sag or pike.
exercises.notes: This exercise challenges your ability to resist unwanted movement and helps improve overall body control.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Hip Bridge
exercises.description: Glute activation with an unstable base

setup.text: Lie on your back with your heels on top of a stability ball and your arms flat at your sides.

instructions.text: Press through your heels to lift your hips into a straight line from shoulders to heels. Hold briefly at the top, resisting any wobble, then lower with control.

exercises.cues: Squeeze your glutes at the top; keep the ball as still as you can.
exercises.notes: Uses the same stability ball as the rollout, so no reconfiguration is needed.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Paloff Press
exercises.description: Anti-rotation core with a balance demand

setup.text: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and stand side-on to it, holding the band with both hands at your sternum.

instructions.text: Lift the leg closest to the anchor, then press the band straight out in front of your chest and resist the pull that wants to rotate you. Bring your hands back to your chest and repeat before switching sides.

exercises.cues: Stay square to the front; the band should not twist you.
exercises.notes: Standing on one leg adds a balance challenge to the anti-rotation work.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart

setup.text: Stand tall holding a resistance band in front of you at shoulder height with your hands about shoulder-width apart.

instructions.text: Pull the band apart by driving your hands out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Keep your arms straight, then return slowly to the start.

exercises.cues: Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
exercises.notes: Uses the same band as the Paloff press, so pair them.

exercises.name: Wall Sit

setup.text: Stand with your back against a wall and walk your feet out about two feet in front of you.

instructions.text: Slide down the wall until your knees are bent at about ninety degrees. Hold the position with your back flat against the wall and your weight in your heels.

exercises.cues: Keep your knees over your ankles, not past your toes.
exercises.notes: Needs no equipment at all, so it fits anywhere in a sequence.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge

setup.text: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips.

instructions.text: Step one foot back and lower until both knees are bent at about ninety degrees. Drive through your front heel to return to standing, then alternate sides.

exercises.cues: Keep your torso upright; step back far enough that your front knee stays over your ankle.
exercises.notes: Bodyweight by default; hold a weight to make it harder.
